stemMd: Why does the author discuss different interpretations of repeated loans?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To argue that surveys cannot contain useful information.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To show why a simple activity count may not measure the service’s value.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To prove that frequent borrowers should be banned.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To show that tool quality never matters.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To establish that ownership is always preferable to borrowing.

explanationMd: The final contrast shows that the same loan count can arise from very different experiences. A count does not distinguish useful repeated work from difficulties using equipment. It therefore supports the managers’ reluctance to use volume as the sole success measure.

distractorRationale.c: The author allows repeated loans to reflect useful work.
distractorRationale.d: Difficulty of use is explicitly one possible explanation.
distractorRationale.a: The survey helps reveal an unexpected benefit.
distractorRationale.e: The passage defends several benefits of access.
